research_question: Can a target-separated post-discovery reranker repair semantic region correspondence while retaining every r2 family, including rare families excluded by the conservative r3 claim gate?
hypothesis: A calibrated pair scorer fitted only on high-confidence r3 supports from non-audit parents will rank visually corresponding r2 regions more reliably than foreground DINO nearest-neighbour by combining DINO foreground, DINO box and SigLIP2 crop evidence plus view-disagreement and simple geometry.
mechanism_decision: Keep the class-free r2 partition as the discovery layer, learn only a post-discovery correspondence scorer from r3 supports, and never pass an audit target or query family assignment to the scorer.
closest_baseline: DINOv3-L foreground nearest-neighbour over the complete active r2 region reference bank with query-parent exclusion.
fit_supervision: pre-existing r3 high-confidence descriptive supports; this is disclosed post-discovery supervision, not unsupervised discovery
fit_exclusion: all 42 audit parent IDs are excluded from scorer fitting and threshold calibration
retrieval_reference_policy: all 6514 active r2 regions remain eligible; only the query parent and exact-image duplicates are removed per query
primary_metric: top-1 recovery of the original r2 family among the 16 audit regions whose semantic correspondence is visually supported
secondary_metrics: top-5 r2-family recovery on visually supported audit regions
coverage and precision after a threshold selected only on parent-held-out r3 validation queries
manual visual adjudication of the retrieved query-candidate pairs
negative_control: ambiguous, unsupported and shortcut audit regions are not counted as positive semantic matches
compute: local CPU only over immutable cached arrays; no GPU inference or feature extraction
stop_rule: Do not claim improvement from family-ID recovery alone; inspect retrieved original-photo and region evidence before selecting a flagship relation.
